page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.2xlarge is a storage-focused virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor with 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes an L3 cache of 33 MB. A defining characteristic of this instance is its bundled local storage, consisting of 23622 GB of HDD capacity. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the ecs.d1.2xlarge is optimized primarily for high-capacity storage density rather than raw computational speed. In CPU evaluations, the instance registers in the bottom 25% for both single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, alongside an average PassMark CPU score. Memory performance is similarly constrained, with read-only bandwidth tests placing in the bottom 25%, though large-block write bandwidth achieves an average rating. Cryptographic and compression tasks, such as single-threaded gzip and bzip3 decompression, perform in the bottom 10% to 25% tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.d1.2xlarge offers high local storage density per resource unit, making it a viable option for workloads requiring massive data capacity without demanding high-performance compute. However, the older Intel Xeon processor architecture and lower benchmark scores represent a clear tradeoff for compute-intensive tasks. This instance is best suited for cold data storage, large-scale log archiving, data warehousing, and sequential-access storage workloads where capacity is prioritized over high IOPS or rapid CPU processing.
